newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: COURT BACKS BORBIDGE ON HIGH COURT CHANGES
West Australian Premier, Richard Court, has echoed his Queensland counterpart's calls for changes in the way High Court judges are appointed.
Rob Borbidge says the High Court is an embarrassment which should be made more accountable.
Mr Borbidge says judges should be appointed for fixed terms, Australians should be allowed a say in their appointment, and a mechanism should be implemented to allow judges to be sacked.
Mr Court says he supports changes to the way judges are appointed, and understands concerns that the High Court is too active in its interpretation of the law.
He says people get concerned when the High Court's interpretation of the law verges on setting the law.
OLSEN WELCOMES TARIFF TALK, BUT REMAINS DEFIANT

The South Australian Premier says he won't compromise on motor industry tariffs unless his state's position is protected. But John Olsen says he's encouraged by reports the Commonwealth may be ready to compromise on plans to cut tariffs.
Tariffs in the industry are set to fall to 15 per cent by the year 2000, but the Federal Government's Productivity Commission wants a reduction to five per cent by 2005.
The South Australian Government says tariffs mustn't fall below 15 per cent until the year 2010.
The Federal Industry Department is said to be pushing for a compromise, under which tariffs would fall from 15 per cent to five per cent in the 10 years from the year 2000.
Mr Olsen says car industry tariffs have already fallen from 57 per cent, and the industry has done its bit.
EYE SURGERY FOR ADELAIDE SOCCER PLAYER
Melbourne Police and Soccer Australia are investigating rock throwing incidents which have led to an Adelaide soccer player needing more surgery to try to save an eye.
Fragments of glass became imbedded in 21-year-old Angelo Costanzo's left eye when South Melbourne fans pelted rocks at the team's bus on Sunday night.
Surgery on the eye on Sunday night has proved unsuccessful, and the Adelaide midfielder will undergo more surgery at the Royal Melbourne Hospital.
A linesman was also pelted with missiles during the match at the South Melbourne ground.
CALL FOR ABORIGINAL COMMUNITIES TO DEAL WITH LAW BREAKERS
An indigenous summit is recommending Aboriginal communities be given responsibility for dealing with indigenous people who break the law.
The summit says seven years after the Black Deaths in Custody Royal Commission, incarceration rates have increased by almost 70 per cent.
Aboriginal lawyer Michael Mansell says the Commonwealth should provide resources for Aboriginal communities to develop mechanisms that divert people away from the courts.
He also says benchmarks need to be set for Government action on Aboriginal deaths in custody.
The recommendations will go to the May summit of federal and state ministers with responsibility for indigenous affairs and the criminal justice system.
COURT SUPPORTS PAEDOPHILE IDENTIFICATION
West Australian Premier, Richard Court, says sex offenders should be named as part of their punishment when they are convicted.
Mr Court is supporting the publication of a book containing the names, ages, occupations and home suburbs of convicted sex offenders and paedophiles.
The book is released today.
Mr Court says preying on children is the lowest form of crime.
He says once people have been convicted, there's no reason why information about their convictions shouldn't remain in the public domain.
But he says care needs to be taken to ensure the information is correct.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
